This is an arcade-style basketball game, but it is not coin-operated. It would fall under heading 9504 (articles for arcade, table or parlor games), or possibly 9506 (sports equipment). CBP rulings on similar arcade basketball games for home use have classified them in 9504.90.6000 (other table or parlor games), or 9504.50 (video game consoles) if applicable. This one is electronic, but it is not a video game.

Subheading 9504.90.40 covers game equipment of a kind used in bowling alleys and other such equipment. 9504.90.60 covers "other" games, and 9504.90.9080 was the older statistical suffix. The current HTS has 9504.90.60 as "Other: Table games, parlor games...", with 9504.90.6000 as the full code.

I'm fairly confident that CBP ruled on the Titan Basketball Game as 9504.90.6000, since it is a game with scoring that is played indoors.

{"hts_code": "9504.90.6000", "reason": "An indoor electronic two-player arcade basketball game with scoreboard and game modes is an article for arcade/parlor games of heading 9504, falling in the residual 'other' subheading 9504.90.60."}
